Hence all irreducible factors of A must be distinct even‑index cyclotomic polynomials (x‑powers allowed). No repeated factors. Count all products of distinct Φₙ (n even) with degree ≤8, then multiply by x^r (0≤r≤8−deg). Each yields a unique α; zero excluded. Compute number of such α. The condition “exactly two 1’s” ⇔ ∃k≠l with A·B = x^k+x^l = x^k(1+x^{l−k}). Thus A must divide a monomial times (1+x^d). Hence every irreducible factor of A must be a distinct even‑index cyclotomic polynomial (x‑powers allowed, no repeats).  

So shifty α are exactly those polynomials of the form x^r·∏_{n∈E}Φ_n, where each n is even, Φ_n distinct, and r+deg(∏Φ_n)≤8. Count all such choices (exclude the zero polynomial).  

Pitfalls: allow monomial shifts (x^r), ignore sign (unit ±1), require no repeated cyclotomic factors (since 1+x^d is square‑free), and respect degree ≤8. Compute the number of subsets of even‑index cyclotomics with total degree ≤8 and sum over admissible r. This yields the answer.
